summary.headline: Brahmaputra Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.24% YoY to Rs 110.79 crore, with PAT up 9.57% to Rs 16.48 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated top line crossed Rs 110 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 20.24% YoY and 17.95% QoQ, driven by EPC activity. Consolidated EBITDA rose 13.08% YoY to Rs 25.15 crore, while PAT grew 9.57% YoY to Rs 16.48 crore. Management said Rs 429 crore of orders were booked in the quarter and the order book stands at about Rs 1,600 crore, with roughly 50% yet to start. Management also addressed cash conversion, pointing to Rs 165 crore of OCCPS repayments from June 2027 and arbitration recoveries of Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.04% in Q4 FY26 (as stated on call)

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Consolidated EPC revenue Rs 104.47 crore (vs Rs 87.53 crore in the prior quarter as stated on call); consolidated PBT Rs 14.71 crore (vs Rs 11.43 crore QoQ).

segments.name: Real Estate & Other Income
segments.commentary: Consolidated real estate revenue Rs 6.33 crore, up about 65% YoY from Rs 3.82 crore; real estate PBT Rs 5.40 crore. Management cites 85-90% margins for this segment.

guidance_outlook: Management targets FY27 order book of about Rs 2,500 crore by year-end, against roughly Rs 1,600 crore currently.
Management expects a historic top line and bottom line in FY27 and said it will keep EPC growth at the rate of the last 2-3 years.
Management expects no margin compression for FY28-FY29 and says growth will come from higher order inflow.
Around 80% of the Rs 800 crore-plus order book to be executed over 18 months is expected to bill in the first year, per management.
New mixed-use shopping mall (Rs 500-700 crore valuation) to start construction by year-end; first phase rent yield from FY29-FY30, with three-phase rental target of Rs 50-60 crore annually.
Tax rate expected to rise to 20-22% after 2028 once Section 43B deductions on past interest run off; FY27 effective rate 12-15%.
capex_capacity: Current order book about Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months.
Bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore; focus on railways, institutional buildings (universities, medical colleges), and flood and slope protection works.
Ramping up flood protection technical team by recruiting more engineers.
Balance sheet: bank guarantee limit Rs 100 crore and CC limit Rs 100 crore; soft surety bond limit about Rs 50 crore, enabling bids of up to Rs 1,000 crore more.

Land and assets: about 4 lakh sq ft of shopping mall area, industrial park on 100-200 acres, 30-35 bigha land parcel; land value Rs 100-200 crore and City Centre valuation Rs 600-700 crore (management estimate).
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 order inflow of Rs 429 crore across railways, roads and highway maintenance; over Rs 300 crore booked in the last 75 days.

Major orders: Rs 140 crore road-over-bridge for Northern Central Railway; Rs 81.98 crore staff quarters for NF Railway; Rs 70.18 crore five-year O&M from MoRTH on a Mizoram NHAI corridor; Rs 25.78 crore Assam road maintenance from NHIDCL.
Management says it is selective on bids and avoids hyper-competitive volume work; about 50% of the order book is outside Northeast India.
Wayside Amenities (NHAI land leases, 30-year) bids pending; results expected next month.
Management states that cash-flow issues are concentrated in pre-2020 legacy projects now in arbitration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the executable order book for FY27 and FY28, and what is the bid pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book of Rs 1,600 crore plus, executable over 18-30 months; bid pipeline about Rs 2,500 crore, focused on railways, institutional buildings and flood/slope protection.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash conversion improve given large receivables, WIP, retention and OCCPS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no stuck-up money or slow-moving WIP on post-2020 projects; debtors about Rs 15-20 crore with 45-90 day billing cycles. Pre-2020 legacy projects in arbitration: over Rs 100 crore monetised in five years, about Rs 150 crore still pending, with Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years including bank guarantee releases. OCCPS of Rs 165 crore repayment starts June 2027 and runs to 2034; management plans to swap OCCPS with arbitration awards.

qa_highlights.question: Is real estate a core hedge or to be divested?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans to divest; both segments to operate jointly. Mall development is planned to start by year-end with rental income of Rs 50-60 crore at full three-phase build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Assam floods on ongoing projects?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of works are outside Northeast and unaffected; some Upper Assam projects were affected, but emergency variation works offset this with no negative impact on billing or turnover.

qa_highlights.question: How is pan-India expansion being pursued and does it include light real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is selective, project-by-project; West Bengal is a strategic target. Asset-light real estate via NHAI Wayside Amenities bids is being pursued, with a large Assam bid awaiting results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 12-15% effective rate reflects Section 43B deductions on past interest; expected to move to 20-22% after 2028.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: management acknowledges it is a focus area; Rs 165 crore OCCPS repayments start June 2027 and bank pledge of promoter shares stays until repaid.
Arbitration recoveries of Rs 200-225 crore over two years are management estimates, with timing uncertain.
Flood-related disruption in Upper Assam; management said there was no negative billing impact in Q1.
Real estate and mall project depends on compliances; construction start expected by end-FY27 and rental income only from FY29-FY30.
Tax rate expected to rise to 20-22% after 2028, which will lower PAT growth versus the current 12-15% rate.
Several figures on the call were inconsistent (e.g., order book quoted as Rs 1,000 crore, Rs 1,600 crore and Rs 800 crore; margin figures). Verify against filed results.
key_quotes: In fact, 50% of our current order book is yet to start.
There is no backlog and there is no slow-moving WIP as of date.

So, we are very much confident that in the subsequent quarters, the same momentum with the healthy bottom line will be continue and we keep, expect all the stakeholders support and we are very much sure that in 2026-2027, we will give a historic number from the top line and from the bottom-line point of view.
So, there is no stuck up of money, and currently, we are in a positive cash flow statement position.
summary.management_tone: Management sounded confident and upbeat on order book quality, margins and a historic FY27, repeatedly calling Q1 strong. It was more cautious and less precise on cash conversion, arbitration timing and tax, where answers were hedged and some figures were revised mid-answer.

Industrial park on 100-200 acres (land asset, development timing not given)

growth.why: Management targets a historic top and bottom line in FY27 and an order book rising from about Rs 1,600 cr to Rs 2,500 cr by year-end, backed by Rs 429 cr of Q1 inflow, a named Rs 800 cr-plus order book with ~80% billing in year one, and a bid pipeline of ~Rs 2,500 cr. No explicit FY27 revenue percentage was given.
